changes: INPUTS for Windows: with AB, CD or ABCD on, Windows stopped the Octatrack's audio device with Code 10. The computer now sends its audio at its own clock, the USB timing Windows supports.
Tested on Windows 11 with AB and ABCD; not yet confirmed on a Windows 10 computer or on macOS.
The Octatrack evens out the small speed difference between the computer's clock and its own, one sample at a time and smoothed over a third of a millisecond, so the inputs never run dry or overflow.
INPUTS OFF and every output layout work as before. An Octatrack running 0.4.0 gets this version with its next sync.
Record from your computer into the Octatrack: PROJ > MODWERK > SETTINGS > USB AUDIO > INPUTS sends USB 1/2 to inputs A/B or C/D, or USB 1–4 to all four.
The Octatrack keeps sending its USB outputs while the inputs are on. INPUTS starts OFF, so nothing changes until you choose it.
USB input needs a high-speed connection to a computer. Full speed and Outbox 8 stay output only; without a USB stream the inputs read the jacks.
An Octatrack running USB Audio 0.3.0 gets this version with its next sync. Your layout and Outbox choices stay as they are.
Install USB Audio once and choose layouts in PROJ > MODWERK > SETTINGS > USB AUDIO.
Switch eight track stems between pre-LEVEL and post-LEVEL in both the 16- and 20-channel layouts.
Route any available source or silence to each of the four Outbox 8 USB pairs.
Loading an existing set restores its saved destination, layout and pair assignments.
Track 8/Master reconnects after layout changes and can be kept on the card.
Adds Outbox 8 support and six USB audio output layouts. You pick one before adding the module, and the builder shows its routing and CPU cost.
Supports the Outbox 44.1 kHz handshake and keeps USB MIDI receive, clock and reset. USB settings are saved in backups; older ones keep the twenty-channel layout.
On the Octatrack beta base, USB Audio now syncs over USB: the Load dialog installs the base for your layout.
Documentation only: like every DRAM module it takes about 10 MB of sample memory, so a full project can show OUT OF MEMORY (#433).
Known issue: only the twenty-channel layout has run on a unit, and reports #548, #689, #718, #489 and #462 are still open.
Closes the audio stream cleanly when USB is reset or unplugged.
Reopening the stream no longer plays a tail of the previous session's audio.
Incoming USB MIDI clock now sets the tempo as well, so timestretch, LFOs and effects follow it.
Documentation only: explains that streaming starts from the computer and has no control page on the instrument. The firmware is unchanged.
Can now be built in the browser firmware builder.
First Modwerk catalog release of USB audio output for the track, main and cue streams alongside USB MIDI.
